findings.explanation: implementation and detailedImplementation tell the reader to ingest IIS W3C logs, which carry `time-taken`. The SPL and dataSources expect `sourcetype=dips:arena:applog` with `response_time_ms` and `server_node`. IIS logs onboarded with the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft IIS (Splunkbase 3185) land under that add-on's own sourcetypes and field names, so the search as written returns nothing unless the reader renames the data.
findings.quote: Arena runs on .NET with IIS hosting — enable W3C logging with `time-taken` field and forward via Splunk Universal Forwarder.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one source. If IIS W3C logs are the source, name the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft IIS (Splunkbase 3185), give the sourcetype it assigns, and document the FIELDALIAS or eval mapping from time_taken to response_time_ms and from host or s_computername to server_node. If an Arena application log is the source, say where Arena writes it and drop the IIS instructions.

findings.explanation: The SPL applies one 3000 ms threshold to all requests, has no split by request_url or screen type, and alerts on any single 5-minute bucket. The implementation also says to exclude batch processes and API integrations from clinician-facing p95, but the SPL does not exclude anything.
findings.quote: p95 < 3 seconds for interactive clinical screens, p95 < 1 second for patient lookup. Alert on sustained degradation (3 consecutive 5-minute intervals above threshold).
findings.suggested_fix: Either describe the SPL as it is (single 3 s p95 per server_node per 5-minute bucket, all requests) or note that the reader must add request_url classification, a 1 s threshold for patient lookup, exclusion of batch/API URLs, and a streak condition (for example streamstats over consecutive breaching buckets).

findings.explanation: DIPS's own figure is that its 100,000 users are over 80% of hospital health personnel (not 80% of hospitals), and that it serves all hospitals in Helse Nord, Helse Vest and Helse Sør-Øst, covering about 4.3 million inhabitants. The implementation's 'serves all regional health authorities' is also wrong: Helse Midt-Norge uses Helseplattformen (Epic).
findings.quote: DIPS Arena is Norway's dominant EHR system, serving approximately 80% of Norwegian hospitals with over 100,000 healthcare professionals and 4.3 million patient records.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'used by all hospitals in Helse Nord, Helse Vest and Helse Sør-Øst (about 4.3 million inhabitants; over 80% of hospital clinicians); Helse Midt-Norge uses Helseplattformen/Epic'.

findings.explanation: Step 1 and the 'Understanding this SPL' paragraph are cut off mid-sentence ('degrada…', 'proactive intervention before…'), so the reader loses the threshold and exclusion guidance.
findings.suggested_fix: Render the full implementation text, or summarise it in complete sentences.

findings.explanation: The implementation describes forwarding IIS log files, which is a file monitor input and not a modular input or scripted poll. The listed fields `request_url`, `http_status` and `user_count` are never used, although `request_url` is what the per-screen thresholds would need.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the actual collection (UF monitor of the IIS log directory, or HEC from Arena) and say which field identifies the screen or transaction for threshold splitting.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: T1078 (Valid Accounts) has no relation to application response-time monitoring.
No request-type split, batch/API exclusion or consecutive-interval condition, although the implementation relies on all three. It alerts on a single 5-minute breach.

summary: The domain context is useful, but the implementation describes collecting IIS W3C logs with alerting on sustained degradation and per-screen thresholds, while the SPL reads a custom `dips:arena:applog` sourcetype and fires on any single 5-minute bucket above 3 s. Some DIPS market facts are stated loosely.
